assumptions: Information gain in research can be proxied by model prediction accuracy.
Computational or temporal resource expenditure is measurable.
Abandonment is a rational response to diminishing returns in open-ended scientific inquiry.
definition.falsification: If research questions with low initial prediction accuracy consistently yield high-value breakthroughs without meeting the marginal utility threshold, the threshold model is falsified.
definition.statement: An intelligent agent should abandon a research question when the marginal utility of continued information gain (measured by prediction accuracy improvement over time) falls below a predefined threshold relative to the resource expenditure.
definition.uncertainty: The primary uncertainty is whether 'value' in scientific research can be adequately captured by prediction accuracy alone.

definition.reason: Transitioning to experimental validation of the defined abandonment threshold hypothesis to determine if prediction accuracy improvements track with utility.
definition.stop: If the simulated agent cannot differentiate between saturation and progress in the test environment.
definition.uncertainty: Whether empirical results will distinguish between 'stagnant' inquiries and 'deep' inquiries that appear stagnant but require more time.

proposal.summary: This update formalizes a hypothesis regarding the epistemic thresholds required for autonomous question abandonment, aligning with the project's commitment to quantify these boundaries based on model prediction accuracy.
proposal.title: Defining Epistemic Thresholds for Research Abandonment
